standard_prerequisites: Rational equivalence by locally finite sums of divisors of rational functions on integral closed subspaces of one dimension higher
The preparation formula expressing the flat pullback of a divisor of a rational function as a multiplicity weighted sum of restrictions, and the compatibility of flat pullback with proper pushforward
Local finiteness of the preimages of the subspaces occurring in a rational equivalence, which makes the pulled back sum well defined
core_obligations: Unwind rational equivalence: the difference of the two cycles is a locally finite sum of pushforwards of divisors of rational functions on integral closed subspaces of dimension one higher
Observe that pulling the sum back term by term makes sense because the preimages of the subspaces form a locally finite family

Pass to the fibre products over the subspaces and use the compatibility of flat pullback with proper pushforward to write the pullback of the sum as the sum of the pushforwards of the pulled back divisors
Apply the preparation formula to see that each pulled back divisor is rationally equivalent to zero on its fibre product, hence so is each of its pushforwards
Conclude that the whole locally finite sum is rationally equivalent to zero, which is the required statement
proof_roadmap: Unwind rational equivalence into a locally finite sum of divisors and pull the sum back term by term
Pass to the fibre products and use the projection formula to move the flat pullback inside the sum
Apply the preparation formula term by term and conclude by local finiteness
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is that flat pullback preserves rational equivalence at source lines 2133-2139, label lemma-flat-pullback-rational-equivalence, whose proof occupies source lines 2141-2173. The proof unwinds rational equivalence into a locally finite sum of pushforwards of divisors of rational functions, observes that the pulled back sum is well defined because the preimages of the subspaces stay locally finite, passes to the fibre products over those subspaces and moves the flat pullback inside the sum by the projection formula, and then applies the preparation formula term by term to see that each pulled back divisor is rationally equivalent to zero. Local finiteness is what upgrades the term by term conclusion to the statement. The counted statement records neither the fibre products nor the term by term reduction.
